$comment: Hand-written layer for scripts/sync-testing.mjs. Every sentence here is public language: no names, tools, suppliers, prices or datasheet figures. The exporter takes numbers from the bench app (or the capture files) and takes ALL prose from this file; it never copies a note or finding from the app. A figure's `checks` pin the numbers its finding text quotes, so the export fails when the data and the sentence drift apart. `status: needs-review` figures and timeline items are exported but never rendered.

figures.title: Current sense against clamp reference
figures.blurb: The current-sense amplifier output as the bench controller reads it, against a clamp meter on the battery lead, at six throttle holds. No capture exists after the change that followed.

series.name: Clamp meter on the battery lead

figures.setup: One OpenESC-20x20 on the bench with one motor driven from the bench controller. The ESC trace is the bench controller's ADC reading of the current-sense amplifier output, converted at a set gain of 50 A/V. A DC clamp meter on the battery lead is the reference. Six throttle holds of 8 to 20 s each, from 15 to 100 percent.
figures.finding: The sense reading does not track the clamp. At 80 percent throttle it read 11.6 A against the clamp's 32.4 A, and at 100 percent 64.7 A against 55.7 A: the error changes size and direction with throttle. At 15 percent it read 1.03 A against 0.39 A, but the clamp reads -0.43 A with no current flowing and that offset is not removed, so the low-throttle ratio is not reliable.
caveats: One unit, one run.
The ESC trace is a bench controller ADC value at a set gain, not a reading from the ESC firmware.
The clamp's zero offset (-0.43 A, median of the idle frames) is not removed.
The clamp is reference grade below 40 A; the 100 percent point is above that.
No capture exists after the rev3.2 input network, so this figure shows the state before the change only. Whether the change removed the error is not known.

source.reduction: One median per throttle hold over the settled window; frames in throttle or speed transients are excluded.

figures.title: Die temperature in a ramp to destruction
figures.blurb: Die temperature against clamp current while one channel was ramped to full throttle with no thermal guard.
figures.setup: One OpenESC-20x20, channel 4 driven alone. Throttle ramped from 0 to full over 120 s with the thermal limit disabled, fan cooling and a fresh pack. The plot ends where the bus voltage telemetry reads zero.
figures.finding: The die reading rose from 23 C to 156 C while the clamp current climbed to 39.8 A. From about 100.1 s the electrical speed fell by about 43 percent (45000 to 25700 erpm in 0.6 s) and the clamp current fell to about 10 A; the motor kept turning. The die reading peaked at 161 C 1.4 s after the 156 C point. Bus voltage telemetry reads zero from 104 s.
caveats: Single channel, one unit, run to destruction with no thermal guard.
The die sensor is the controller's own temperature sensor, not a measurement of the output transistors.
Why the speed and current fell at about 100.1 s is not established by this capture.
The clamp reads about -0.85 A with no current flowing; the offset is not removed.
The die reading stays at 156 C once telemetry is lost; the plot ends where that starts.

source.reduction: Logged frames from 8 s to the loss of bus voltage telemetry, kept as the minimum and maximum of 170 time buckets.

figures.title: Current sense against clamp reference, 30x30
figures.blurb: The ESC's own current reading against a clamp meter during a throttle sweep.

series.name: Clamp meter on the battery lead

figures.setup: One OpenESC-30x30 driving four motors on a 13 inch load rig, throttle swept up and back down. A DC clamp meter on the battery lead is the reference. The plot stops at the last throttle bin with a clamp reading (86 A; the clamp's range is 100 A).
figures.finding: Where the clamp reads, the ESC read 1.16 to 1.46 times the clamp in each throttle bin, between 1.25 and 1.35 in 26 of 36 bins.
caveats: One sweep on one board.
That the board is an OpenESC-30x30 is the operator's statement; its revision is not in the capture.
Up and down legs of the sweep differ by up to 10 A.
Held for founder review before publication.

source.reduction: Sweep bins of mechanical speed; up and down legs averaged in each bin.

figures.title: Thrust against rotor speed
figures.blurb: Thrust stand sweep from 10 to 100 percent throttle in ten holds, with the motor not recorded.
figures.setup: Thrust stand. The load-cell scale is the controller's stored value, not checked against a known weight. Ten throttle holds of about 4 s from 10 to 100 percent. Motor, propeller, ESC and pack are not recorded for the 13:25 UTC run; the 13:16 UTC run lists its motor as OpenMotor-2306. Rotor speed is the ESC's electrical speed divided by 7 pole pairs, the default pole count stored in the capture. The motor's real pole count is not recorded, so the rpm axis depends on that assumption.
figures.finding: From 40 percent throttle up, thrust is about 1.7 g per krpm squared (1.67 to 1.74 in the 13:25 UTC run), taking the stored 7 pole pairs as correct. That run, with no motor recorded, reaches 1496 g at 100 percent throttle and 29350 rpm. At the same speed the 13:16 UTC run reads 2 to 3 percent less thrust, with a pack voltage up to 1.9 V higher.
caveats: One capture per run; the 13:25 UTC run was not repeated.
Motor, propeller, ESC and pack are not recorded for the 13:25 UTC run.
The clamp meter was not recorded.
The load-cell scale comes from the controller's stored value; no independent weight check is recorded in the capture.

The 13:16 UTC run ends at 70 percent: the pack was pulled during the 80 percent step, so its later holds are dropped. The 13:25 UTC run was recorded after the bench controller was changed to abort in that case.

source.reduction: Median of the last 2 s of each throttle hold; the band is the 25th to 75th percentile over the same window. Holds with no pack voltage reading are dropped.

figures.title: Rotor speed by throttle
figures.blurb: Rotor speed at each throttle hold.
figures.setup: Same two thrust stand runs as the thrust figure. Rotor speed is the ESC's electrical speed divided by 7 pole pairs, the default pole count stored in the capture; the motor's real pole count is not recorded.
figures.finding: Rotor speed rises from about 5000 rpm at 10 percent to 29350 rpm at 100 percent in the 13:25 UTC run, taking 7 pole pairs as correct.
caveats: One capture per run.
Motor, propeller, ESC and pack are not recorded for the 13:25 UTC run.

source.reduction: Median of the last 2 s of each throttle hold. Holds with no pack voltage reading are dropped.

figures.title: Thrust by throttle
figures.setup: Same two thrust stand runs as the thrust figure. The load-cell scale is the controller's stored value, not checked against a known weight.
figures.finding: Thrust is 30 g at 10 percent and 1496 g at 100 percent in the 13:25 UTC run.
caveats: One capture per run.
At 10 percent the 13:25 UTC run reads 30 g and the 13:16 UTC run 35 g, a difference of about 17 percent at a low load.
The clamp meter was not recorded.
No independent weight check of the load cell is recorded.

source.reduction: Median of the last 2 s of each throttle hold. Holds with no pack voltage reading are dropped.

figures.title: Pack voltage by throttle
figures.blurb: Pack voltage at each throttle hold.
figures.setup: Same two thrust stand runs as the thrust figure. Pack voltage is read by the ESC.
figures.finding: The pack sags from 24.4 V at 10 percent to 19.3 V at 100 percent in the 13:25 UTC run. The 13:16 UTC run starts about 0.3 V higher and is 1.9 V higher at 70 percent.
caveats: The packs are not recorded; the 13:16 UTC run reads higher throughout.
Voltage is the ESC's own reading, not checked against a meter.

source.reduction: Median of the last 2 s of each throttle hold. Holds with no pack voltage reading are dropped.

figures.title: ESC temperature by throttle
figures.blurb: Hottest ESC die reading at each throttle hold.
figures.setup: Same two thrust stand runs as the thrust figure. Temperature is the hottest of the ESC's reported die readings.
figures.finding: The hottest die reading rises from 44 C at 10 percent to 72 C at 100 percent in the 13:25 UTC run; the 13:16 UTC run stays between 42 and 48 C up to 70 percent.
caveats: The 13:25 UTC run was hotter at the same throttle; motor, propeller, cooling and packs are not recorded.
The die sensor is the controller's own, not a measurement of the output transistors.

source.reduction: Median of the last 2 s of each throttle hold. Holds with no pack voltage reading are dropped.

figures.title: RSSI against distance, Gemini and Mono
figures.blurb: One 75 minute ride out to 5.3 km with a Gemini and a Mono on the same carry. Reported RSSI here; link quality is in the next figure.
figures.setup: One OpenRX-Gemini and one OpenRX-Mono on the same carry, logged together during a ride out along a road to 5.3 km. Distance is measured from the start of the GPS track, not from the transmitter.
figures.finding: From 2.9 km to 5.3 km the Gemini's reported RSSI is below the Mono's in 24 of the 25 100 m bins that both logged and equal in one: a median of 4 dB lower, up to 7 dB, and 2 dB or more lower in 23 of the 25. In the same bins its link quality is higher than the Mono's in all 25, by a median of 15 points, so the Gemini reported a weaker signal and held the link better. Below 1.3 km the two RSSI values are within about 5 dB of each other in either direction.
caveats: One unit of each, one ride.
Antenna placement on the carry may explain the RSSI gap.
RSSI is the value each receiver reports after its own antenna selection.
The receiver columns in the log are numbered, not named; which column is which unit comes from the operators' notes. One column duplicates the Mono and is excluded.
Transmitter settings and receiver firmware are not recorded.
No transmitter position or terrain is recorded, so range is not line-of-sight range.

source.reduction: Median of the logged RSSI in 100 m distance bins; the band is the 25th to 75th percentile.

figures.title: Link quality against distance, Gemini and Mono
figures.blurb: The same ride as the RSSI figure: link quality of the Gemini and the Mono in 100 m distance bins.
figures.setup: One OpenRX-Gemini and one OpenRX-Mono on the same carry, logged together during a ride out along a road to 5.3 km. Distance is measured from the start of the GPS track, not from the transmitter.
figures.finding: From 2.9 km to 5.3 km the Gemini's link quality is higher than the Mono's in all 25 of the 100 m bins that both logged, by a median of 15 points and up to 48. This is the metric on which the Gemini leads while its reported RSSI is lower.
caveats: One unit of each, one ride.
The receiver columns in the log are numbered, not named; which column is which unit comes from the operators' notes. One column duplicates the Mono and is excluded.
Transmitter settings and receiver firmware are not recorded.
No transmitter position or terrain is recorded, so range is not line-of-sight range.
Link quality is each receiver's own figure; the two may not be computed identically.

source.reduction: Median of the logged link quality in 100 m distance bins; the band is the 25th to 75th percentile.

figures.title: Link quality and RSSI at the first link drop
figures.blurb: RSSI and link quality of the Lite as the ride passed out of range for the first time.
figures.setup: One OpenRX-Lite in the same ride as the distance figure, 120 s around the first link drop.
figures.finding: RSSI fell from -74 dBm at 284 s to -98 dBm at 294.5 s. Link quality held at 87 percent or more until 292.6 s, then fell to 17 percent at 305.8 s, when RSSI had reached -104 dBm. An earlier dip to -91 dBm at 263 s cost link quality only 10 points and recovered.
caveats: One unit, one ride.
That this column is the Lite follows the operators' hand markers; the log does not name its receivers.
Transmitter settings and receiver firmware are not recorded.

source.reduction: Logged values from 200 s to 320 s, unreduced.

figures.title: Gemini antenna 2 use against distance
figures.blurb: How often the Gemini selected its second antenna along the ride.

series.name: Share of logged samples on antenna 2

figures.setup: One OpenRX-Gemini, same ride as the distance figure. The log records which of its two antennas was active in each sample.
figures.finding: Antenna 2 is not selected in the first 1 km. Its share is 10 to 16 percent of samples between 1.5 and 4 km, 22 percent from 4.5 to 5 km and 35 percent from 5 km to the end of the track.
caveats: One unit, one ride.
Samples are not evenly spread over distance: bins hold 9 to 871 samples, and bins with fewer than 8 are dropped.
Antenna placement and orientation are not recorded.

source.reduction: Share of logged samples with antenna 2 active in 500 m distance bins.

figures.title: ESC die temperature in flight, three airframes
figures.blurb: ESC die temperature in the hottest retained flight of each of three airframes, logged by an OpenFC-Lite on 2026-08-09.
figures.setup: Blackbox logs from three airframes flown on 2026-08-09 with an OpenFC-Lite (RP2350B) and the ESC die temperature reported over telemetry. For each airframe, the retained flight with the highest die reading is shown; the 8 inch is shown on both 6S and 8S. A 3 inch airframe flew on a different board variant and is not shown.
figures.finding: The highest die reading was 52.6 C on the 5 inch freestyle, 64.0 C on the 5 inch race, 87.4 C on the 8 inch on 6S and 116 C on the 8 inch on 8S.
caveats: This is a flight log from one day, not a flight controller bench measurement. No FC bench capture exists.
The flights are the hottest of the retained logs, not a sample of typical flights, and the retained logs are a selection of 103.
The die sensor is the ESC's own, not a measurement of the output transistors; the ESC model and cooling are not recorded in the log.
Flight length, load and ambient temperature differ between the airframes, so the curves are not a like-for-like comparison.

source.reduction: Logged ESC die temperature, kept as the minimum and maximum of 150 time buckets per flight.

timeline.tested: Thrust map on the new thrust stand: ten throttle holds from 10 to 100 percent.
timeline.saw: In the 13:25 UTC run thrust reached 1496 g at 100 percent throttle; motor, propeller, ESC and pack were not recorded. In the earlier 13:16 UTC run a pack was pulled during the 80 percent step and the throttle profile kept stepping up to full.
timeline.changed: The bench controller now aborts the run when the pack is pulled, and the 13:25 UTC run was recorded with that change. The thrust stand test plans no longer include a current cut, because current sense on the stand is not calibrated.

timeline.tested: Continuous current rating by stepping to a fixed current and waiting for the die temperature to settle.
timeline.saw: Calculated from the fitted thermal time constant of 5 to 10 minutes, not captured: a fixed-current step on a pack cannot reach thermal steady state, because 20 s at the target current gives only a few percent of the steady temperature rise.
timeline.changed: The bench now holds a target die temperature and reads the current needed to hold it.

timeline.tested: Review of the scope captures from the destructive ramp session.
timeline.saw: Scope channel 1 read one constant value in all nine sessions of that afternoon and no check flagged it.

timeline.tested: Throttle sweep against a clamp reference.
timeline.saw: The current-sense amplifier reading, as read by the bench controller, did not track the clamp: 11.6 A against 32.4 A at 80 percent throttle, and 64.7 A against 55.7 A at 100 percent.
timeline.changed: An input network was added to the current-sense amplifier in rev3.2. It has not been tested on hardware: no capture after the change exists.

timeline.tested: One channel ramped from 0 to full throttle with no thermal guard.
timeline.saw: Clamp current peaked at 39.8 A with the die sensor at 156 C. The die reading reached 161 C and bus voltage telemetry then stopped.

timeline.tested: First boards flashed for the bench.
timeline.saw: Boards left the flashing step with the temperature limit at 255 and a default motor preset.
timeline.changed: Both are now set per product in the flashing jig.

timeline.tested: First flights of the full stack on five drones.
timeline.saw: 103 blackbox logs from four of the drones, about half of them arm and disarm blips. The fifth drone's SD card failed after the session. On the 8 inch, seven logs were recorded with the FC on a separate battery, so their voltage is not pack voltage.

timeline.tested: Ride out to 5.3 km with a Gemini and a Mono on the same carry.
timeline.saw: Beyond 2.9 km the Gemini's reported RSSI was below the Mono's in 24 of the 25 100 m bins and equal in one, by a median of 4 dB and up to 7 dB. Its link quality was higher in all 25 bins, by a median of 15 points. The log numbers its receivers instead of naming them, so the column-to-unit mapping was taken from the operators' notes and one duplicate column was excluded.
